Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

further adverb and adjective

farther, to a greater distance

also farther, further on, further away, further back

classical

Ter. Heaut. 212: vidē sīs nē quō hinc abeās longius
Phaedr. App. 19.6: satis est, inquit, sī recēdis longius
Sen. Ep. 40.7: longius quam voluit effertur

longius

adverb, comparative of longē

further, farther

Other words

  • ultrā — further, beyond; any further

    adverb; also a preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Quint. 2.3.7: nec prōcēdat ultrā quam comes possit; Tac. Agr. 30.5: nūlla jam ultrā gēns

  • ulterior, ulterius — further, farther (the one beyond)

    adjective, comparative, declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.7; Cic. Prov. Cons. 36: Gallia ulterior, Further Gaul (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Tū, ut tempus est diēī, vidē sīs nē quō hinc abeās longius.

    You, seeing the time of day, mind you don’t wander off any further.Ter. Heaut. 212

  • ut vēlōcissimus quoque, sī forte iter cum parvulō faciat, det manum et gradum suum minuat nec prōcēdat ultrā quam comes possit

    as even the fastest walker, if he happens to be travelling with a little child, gives him his hand, shortens his stride and goes no further than his companion canQuint. 2.3.7

  • satis est, inquit, sī recēdis longius

    “it’s enough,” she said, “if you stand further back”Phaedr. App. 19.6

See also further, forward.
